directives.meaning: Make the point with a concrete example.

sentences.text: The art of the Indus Valley Civilisation, which emerged in the second half of the third millennium BCE, spanned stone, bronze, terracotta, seals, pottery and jewellery.
The steatite bust of a bearded 'priest-king' from Mohenjodaro wears a shawl with trefoil patterns over the left shoulder.
The bronze Dancing Girl from Mohenjodaro, cast by the lost-wax technique, stands with her right hand on her hip and her left arm covered in bangles.
Seals, mostly of steatite and carved in intaglio, depict animals such as the unicorn bull, tiger and elephant along with an undeciphered script.
The so-called Pashupati seal shows a cross-legged figure surrounded by an elephant, a tiger, a rhinoceros and a buffalo.
Terracotta was used for mother goddess figurines and toys such as carts, whistles and rattles.
Wheel-made red pottery painted in black, and bead workshops at Chanhudaro and Lothal using carnelian and lapis lazuli, show high technical skill.
Lost-wax casting and terracotta craft survive in India today, a Harappan legacy worth documenting.
